pr.title: Add project console, a terminal list of every live session that answers and discusses its items and pull requests
pr.head: b27132ffc91fd2bb483750154d4dcfd173209870

summary: Projector keeps pull request subscriptions and inbox items for each agent session. This layer adds project console, a terminal interface that lists live sessions and lets you open one session to answer items, send messages, and read its conversation.

The console records choices through the existing inbox functions and leaves delivery to each session’s own deliverer. Messages are one way: the agent answers in its normal conversation. A collapsed-by-default conversation section reads only human prompts, delivered inbox lines, and assistant text from the host’s local transcript.

cards.title: What the console shows
cards.html:
• Session: one Claude Code or Codex conversation with live delivery.
  • Inbox item: a question, request, notice, or one-way message stored for that session.
  • Drawer: expanded detail and actions below a selected item or pull request.
  • Transcript: the local JSON Lines file the host writes for its conversation.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: The configured gate, exact-head CI, metadata checks, and 442 focused tests passed. The earlier long-drawer issue remains fixed. One testing-rule finding remains: the conversation test class inherits and reruns three scrolling tests already collected in their own class.

groups.title: Read the host conversation without its internal records
groups.kicker: A bounded first read and incremental tail turn transcript entries into speech.
intro: The new reader finds the Claude Code transcript or the Codex rollout registered for a session. It starts with at most the last 2 MiB, waits for incomplete JSON lines to finish, then reads only appended bytes. Replacing or truncating the transcript resets the reader.

Each host parser keeps the person’s text, the inbox lines sent on their behalf, and assistant text. Tool calls, results, reasoning, host instructions, and Projector pull request events are omitted. Made-up fixtures exercise both host formats without publishing real conversations.

files.note: Finds and incrementally reads session transcripts, filtering each host’s record format.

groups.title: Browse sessions and follow a conversation
groups.kicker: The terminal model records choices and shows a per-session chat section.
intro: The home list orders sessions by open questions and requests. A session panel shows cached pull requests, inbox items, and a conversation heading. Pressing v expands the conversation for that session, starts at its newest line, and follows new text until you scroll back.

Conversation reads run in the background only while shown. The console retains the newest 400 speech entries per session. Page keys scroll tall drawers or the conversation without closing them, and ordinary row movement still closes a drawer.

files.note: Session refresh, input, recording actions, conversation visibility, follow behavior, and terminal rendering.

checks.text: The 442-test focused run covers session-specific recording, conversation visibility and follow behavior, delivery integration, and the earlier scrolling regression.

files.note: Exercises the console model and real renderer with temporary state and a fake terminal.

checks.text: Conversation inherits the three scrolling tests from Scrolling, so unittest collects those exact methods twice. Extract shared test-free setup helpers and leave each scrolling case in one class, as testing.md § 4 requires.

groups.title: Expose the command without granting agents answer authority
groups.kicker: Terminal support and permission policy surround the existing recording path.
intro: project console requires a terminal and Python’s curses module. It records through the inbox functions already used by the CLI, and wakes Codex delivery through the existing helper.

Because the console records the person’s answers and messages, Claude Code asks before an agent starts it. Codex’s automatic allow list leaves it to normal approval. The revised policy no longer carries the removed reply/read command surface.
